post.caption: Warriors once decorated shields with red coral. The Witham Shield, from Iron Age Britain, has Mediterranean coral, and the Roman writer Pliny said Gauls decorated swords with it too. Red coral is the hard skeleton of tiny sea animals called polyps, and scientists only accepted coral as an animal in the 1700s. A branch thickens by only a fraction of a millimeter a year, and colonies can live for about a century. Licensed scuba divers harvest it 50 meters down or deeper. The red comes from organic pigments in the skeleton. Coral rattles were once teething toys and charms for babies. Torre del Greco in Italy has worked coral for over two centuries.
